addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

content.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/hcengineering/platform
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: hardcoreeng/front:v0.7.426 (plus account, transactor, workspace, collaborator, fulltext, rekoni, stats, kvs, and cockroach, redpanda, elastic, minio, nginx)
  port: 80
  vm: m1.mem16
  flavor_id: "7"
  database: none. Huly's datastore is CockroachDB, which redu does not offer managed, so it runs on the app VM on a named volume
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0556
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: huly
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE COMPOSE YOU WANT IS IN A DIFFERENT REPO FROM THE ONE THIS FILE CREDITS. hcengineering/platform is the source code, and dev/docker-compose.yaml in it is a 732-line DEVELOPMENT stack with a redpanda console and every optional service: do not deploy it. The supported self-host path is hcengineering/huly-selfhost, whose compose.yml is 281 lines and 14 active services, pinned by its .template.huly.conf to HULY_VERSION v0.7.426. Start there, and read MIGRATION.md in that repo before ever changing the version, because Huly upgrades sometimes need steps."
  - "⛔ IT FITS ON ONE VM, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES THE NUMBER, WHICH IS RARE. The huly-selfhost README says in its own words that Huly is resource-heavy: minimum 2 vCPU and 8 GB, recommended 4 vCPU and 16 GB or more, and that servers below the minimum may stop responding or fail. So m1.mem16 (4 vCPU / 16 GB) at GBP 0.0556/hr IS the recommended specification, not a guess, and m1.large would only meet the minimum for GBP 0.007/hr less. ⚠️ THE DISK IS THE PART THAT IS NOT COVERED BY THAT QUOTE: m1.mem16 comes with 40 GB, and this stack puts CockroachDB, an Elasticsearch index, a Redpanda log and every uploaded file on it, on top of fourteen images. Put that in front of the user BEFORE sizing, because growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy. This is far ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium: say so before the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO MANAGED DATABASE IN THIS RECIPE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Huly's datastore is CockroachDB, reached over the postgres wire, and redu has no managed CockroachDB. Substituting redu's managed Postgres is NOT a supported configuration: the platform ships a Cockroach-specific adapter for its communication subsystem (foundations/communication/packages/cockroach) and both documented deployments, compose and Helm, run CockroachDB. Do not test that substitution on someone's real workspace. Consequence to state plainly BEFORE they approve: apps, issues, documents and messages all live on the app VM's named volumes, so deleting the deployment deletes them. huly-selfhost ships backup-create.sh and backup-restore.sh; that is the backup story, and it is worth setting up on day one."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: PUBLIC SIGN-UP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT AND THE FIRST PERSON TO SIGN UP GETS AN ACCOUNT AND A WORKSPACE ON YOUR SERVER. There is no install wizard and no deploy-time admin variable, so this needs a TWO-PHASE deploy and you must not stop at 'the URL works'. Phase one: deploy with sign-up open, then IMMEDIATELY create the user's account, having confirmed the email address with them first. Phase two: set DISABLE_SIGNUP=true on BOTH the account AND the front service and restart those two containers. Verified in server/account-service/src/index.ts:137-138: that variable makes getMethods() omit signUp and signUpOtp entirely, so it is a real server-side closure and not a UI toggle, and invite-based joining (signUpJoin) keeps working. Upstream's own README says to create the initial account before disabling sign-ups. The window between healthy and claimed is real: keep it to minutes, and check the account list afterwards."
  - "⛔ SET SECURE AND HOST_ADDRESS OR THE APP LOADS AND THEN CANNOT CONNECT. Their compose builds every public URL with the shell trick http${SECURE:+s}://${HOST_ADDRESS}, so an EMPTY SECURE yields http:// and ws:// links. Behind redu's TLS the browser then blocks them as mixed content and you get a page that renders and never signs in, which reads as a broken deploy rather than a config mistake. Set SECURE=true and HOST_ADDRESS to the bare hostname with no scheme. Generate the dname yourself in the full huly-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so both are known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ SHIP .huly.nginx IN THE TARBALL. IT STARTS WITH A DOT. The compose bind-mounts ./.huly.nginx into the nginx container as its only server block, and it is a committed file in huly-selfhost rather than something generated at boot. If your upload misses dotfiles, nginx starts with the stock default site and every route 404s while all fourteen containers look healthy. Check the tarball actually contains it before deploying. That file is also where the routes live: / to front:8080, /_accounts, /_collaborator, /_transactor, /_rekoni, /_stats, with client_max_body_size 100M."
  - "PORT 80, THROUGH THEIR NGINX, AND NOTHING ELSE. Publish 80 on the host and pass port 80 to deploy_compose. ⚠️ Simplify their publish line: upstream writes \"${HTTP_BIND}:${HTTP_PORT}:80\" and relies on an EMPTY variable meaning all interfaces, which is a footgun in a file you are already editing. Write 80:80. Also DELETE the ports: block on the kvs service, which publishes 8094 on the host: nothing in .huly.nginx routes to it and no other service in this compose is given its URL, so it does not need to be reachable from outside the compose network at all."
  - "⛔ SET SECRET ONCE AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It is passed to every service as SERVER_SECRET or SECRET and it signs the tokens the browser, the transactor and the collaborator all present to each other. Two failure modes, and the second is the confusing one: change it and everybody is logged out; set it INCONSISTENTLY across services and the app loads, signs in, and then the transactor or the collaborator rejects the token, so documents will not open and it looks like a broken feature rather than a broken secret. Upstream's setup script generates it; on redu, generate one long random value yourself and put it in the project .env so every service interpolates the same one."
  - "PIN THE VERSION, AND KNOW WHY THE REGISTRY LOOKS NEWER THAN IT IS. Set HULY_VERSION=v0.7.426, which is the newest GitHub release (2026-07-05) and what huly-selfhost's own template pins. ⚠️ Docker Hub disagrees with GitHub in both directions: hardcoreeng/front carries v0.7.432 (2026-07-16) with NO matching GitHub release, and above that s0.7.433 to s0.7.437, which are STAGING builds. The huly-selfhost README is explicit that self-hosted deployments use v* tags. Do not reach for the newest-looking tag. The supporting images are pinned upstream too: cockroachdb/cockroach:latest-v24.2, redpandadata/redpanda:v24.3.6, elasticsearch:7.14.2, nginx:1.21.3. ⚠️ minio/minio has no tag in their compose, which means :latest, and the newest community MinIO tag on Docker Hub is from 2025-09-07: pin minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z rather than leaving it floating."
  - "PERSIST FIVE NAMED VOLUMES: cr_data and cr_certs (CockroachDB, which is everything), elastic (the search index, rebuildable but slow), files (MinIO: every uploaded document and attachment) and redpanda (the queue). Use NAMED volumes rather than the VOLUME_*_PATH bind-mount option their .conf offers, because a source re-upload replaces the project directory. Losing files loses attachments while the issues referencing them survive, which is the confusing failure; losing cr_data loses the product."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH BEFORE ANYONE SIGNS IN: the front-end bundle, the account service's JSON-RPC endpoint at /_accounts (which is how login and, until you close it, sign-up work), and the /_stats endpoint. MinIO is NOT routed by .huly.nginx and is not published, which is what makes the image-default MinIO credentials embedded in six STORAGE_CONFIG strings survivable rather than fatal. ⚠️ If you ever add a public route to MinIO, change those credentials FIRST, and remember they appear in all six strings, so a partial change breaks file uploads in exactly one service."
  - "IT IS FOURTEEN CONTAINERS AND THE FIRST BOOT IS LONG. Elasticsearch installs its ingest-attachment plugin on first start (their compose does it in the command), CockroachDB initialises its store, Redpanda formats its log, and only then do nine Huly services connect. Give the health check generous room and judge readiness by the account RPC answering, not by nginx answering: nginx is up long before the platform behind it is."
  - "ELASTICSEARCH TAKES 1 GB BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING. Their compose sets ES_JAVA_OPTS to -Xms1024m -Xmx1024m, so a full gigabyte of the VM is committed to the search JVM at boot. That is a large part of why upstream's minimum is 8 GB, and it is the first knob to turn if you ever need room, at the cost of full-text search performance."
  - "THE COMMENTED-OUT SERVICES ARE COMMENTED OUT FOR A REASON. compose.yml ships mongodb, redis and hulypulse disabled, and their comments say what each unlocks: mongo for the aibot and calendar services, redis for HulyPulse, HulyPulse for push notifications and real-time updates. Leave them off for a first deploy. Every one of them is another container on the same VM and the 16 GB above does not include them."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The workspace service runs Huly's own migrations, and the account service migrates its own schema at boot. Do not add a migration step of your own."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost (about GBP 0.056/hr, roughly GBP 41 a month, NOT inside the no-card trial), the fact that the data lives on the app VM and the two-phase sign-up close -> WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '7' (m1.mem16), NO managed database, port 80. Then create their account, then set DISABLE_SIGNUP and restart account and front."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Assemble the compose, the .env and .huly.nginx locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. ⚠️ Do NOT copy huly-selfhost's own .env: its entire contents are the NAME of the conf file their setup script generates, which is not what deploy_compose expects. Write a normal .env with HULY_VERSION, DOCKER_NAME, HOST_ADDRESS, SECURE, TITLE, the CockroachDB variables, the Redpanda variables and SECRET, and skip setup.sh entirely."
  - "LICENCE: EPL-2.0 on both repos, and it is the least demanding thing in this file. Weak copyleft on the modified FILES only, with an explicit patent grant, and no obligation whatsoever on someone running an unmodified build for their own team. Huly also sells a hosted product; self-hosting the open-source build is exactly what these repos exist for."
  - "DELETING IT DELETES THE DATA. There is no managed database left behind: delete_deployment removes the app VM, and CockroachDB, MinIO and the search index go with it. Run huly-selfhost's backup-create.sh and copy the result off the VM first, and say that out loud before running the delete."
---

# Self-host Huly on redu

An all-in-one project management platform (issues, documents, chat, HR, time tracking) on
infrastructure you own: Huly's own self-host stack, fourteen containers, on one memory-first VM
with a public HTTPS URL.

## What this deploys

- **Huly** from its official pinned images: front, account, transactor, workspace, collaborator,
  fulltext, rekoni, stats and kvs.
- **CockroachDB, MinIO, Elasticsearch and Redpanda** beside them, because they are Huly's database,
  file store, search index and queue, and redu offers no managed substitute for any of them.
- Their own nginx as the single ingress on port 80, with redu terminating TLS in front of it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove public sign-up is really off on your Huly, without creating anything.
#   ./verify-signup-closed.sh huly-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed. 1 = OPEN, anyone can create an account right now. 2 = inconclusive, re-run.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-signup-closed.sh <host>}"
RPC="https://$HOST/_accounts"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

rpc_code() {   # $1 = method name. Body on stdin so nothing lands in ps.
  printf '{"method":"%s","params":{}}' "$1" \
    | curl -sS -o "$TMP/out" -w '%{http_code}' \
           -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- "$RPC"
}

# 1. GATE, and the POSITIVE CONTROL in one step. `login` is ALWAYS registered, so if it answers
#    404 we are not talking to Huly's account service and nothing below would mean anything.
code=$(rpc_code login)
case "$code" in
  200|400) echo "gate OK: the account RPC is answering and login is registered." ;;
  502)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from redu's proxy, the stack is still starting." >&2
    echo "  Fourteen containers take a while. Wait and re-run; this is NOT a pass." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  404)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: login itself answered 404, so this is not Huly's account endpoint." >&2
    echo "  Check the nginx route for /_accounts before reading anything into the next step." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  *) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected HTTP $code from the account RPC." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# 2. THE ASSERTION. With DISABLE_SIGNUP=true the method is not registered at all, so the service
#    answers 404 UnknownMethod. Anything else means it IS registered and open to the internet.
code=$(rpc_code signUp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ] && grep -qi 'method' "$TMP/out"; then
  echo "OK: signUp is not registered. Public sign-up is closed at the account service."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUp answered HTTP $code, so the method is still registered." >&2
  echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your server. Set DISABLE_SIGNUP=true" >&2
  echo "  on BOTH the account and front services and restart them, then re-run this." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 3. And the OTP variant, which is a separate method and is easy to forget.
code=$(rpc_code signUpOtp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
  echo "OK: signUpOtp is not registered either."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUpOtp answered HTTP $code and is still open." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Invites still work: signUpJoin stays registered on purpose."

# Self-host Huly on redu

- Their own nginx as the single ingress on port 80, with redu terminating TLS in front of it.

one needs a payment method.

KEEP the redu.md bytes: pass them to get_deployment as redu_md at the end too, so redu merges the old file with the new deploy instead of you overwriting what previous deploys learned.
platform_facts: THE deploy VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. The compose project is named app-src, so containers are app-src-<service>-1 and volumes are app-src_<name>. Use `sudo docker ...` on the VM; podman is not installed. Several deploys rediscovered this independently.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM. Call get_env_keys for the NAMES first (no SSH, values never leave the VM); only if you need an actual VALUE, SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read that one key, `sudo grep '^PGPASSWORD=' /opt/app-src/.env`. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback. ⭐ MEASURED over 38 deploys: of 241 ssh escapes, 146 (61%) were exactly these four things, and the four tools were called 11 times. They are faster than a login, they cost the VM nothing extra (the reading is already cached), and reaching for ssh to run `docker ps` is the single most common wasted minute in a deploy.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

=== compose.yml (281 lines) ===
name: ${DOCKER_NAME}
services:
  nginx:
    image: "nginx:1.21.3"
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_BIND}:${HTTP_PORT}:80"
    volumes:
      - ./.huly.nginx:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - huly_net

  cockroach:
    image: cockroachdb/cockroach:latest-v24.2
    command: start-single-node --accept-sql-without-tls
    environment:
      - COCKROACH_DATABASE=${CR_DATABASE}
      - COCKROACH_USER=${CR_USERNAME}
      - COCKROACH_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}
    volumes:
      - ${VOLUME_CR_DATA_PATH:-cr_data}:/cockroach/cockroach-data
      - ${VOLUME_CR_CERTS_PATH:-cr_certs}:/cockroach/certs
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - huly_net

  redpanda:
    image: docker.redpanda.com/redpandadata/redpanda:v24.3.6
    command:
      - redpanda
      - start
      - --kafka-addr internal://0.0.0.0:9092,external://0.0.0.0:19092
      - --advertise-kafka-addr internal://redpanda:9092,external://localhost:19092
      - --pandaproxy-addr internal://0.0.0.0:8082,external://0.0.0.0:18082
      - --advertise-pandaproxy-addr internal://redpanda:8082,external://localhost:18082
      - --schema-registry-addr internal://0.0.0.0:8081,external://0.0.0.0:18081
      - --rpc-addr redpanda:33145
      - --advertise-rpc-addr redpanda:33145
      - --mode dev-container
      - --smp 1
      - --default-log-level=info
    volumes:
      - ${VOLUME_REDPANDA_PATH:-redpanda}:/var/lib/redpanda/data
    environment:
      - REDPANDA_SUPERUSER_USERNAME=${REDPANDA_ADMIN_USER}
      - REDPANDA_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'rpk', 'cluster', 'info', '-X', 'user=${REDPANDA_ADMIN_USER}', '-X', 'pass=[REDACTED:value]}']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
    networks:
      - huly_net

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Take a backup of a workspace in this local Huly deployment.
# Connection parameters are read from huly_v7.conf (same file docker compose uses).
#
# Backups are incremental: each run only downloads and stores documents that
# are new or changed since the last backup snapshot in <backup-dir> (based on
# per-domain hashes). Re-running this against the same directory is cheap and
# safe - it just adds another snapshot on top of what's already there.
#
# Usage:
#   ./backup-create.sh <backup-dir> <workspace> [options] [-- <extra tool args>]
#
# Options:
#   --full              Force a full recheck: compare every document instead of relying on
#                        stored hashes (slower, use if you suspect the backup is out of sync)
#   --full-verify        Full verification: download and diff every document against the
#                        server, not just changed ones (slowest, most thorough)
#   --force              Force backup even if no transactions changed since last run
#   --include <domains>  ; separated list of domains to include (default: all)
#   --skip <domains>      ; separated list of domains to skip
#   --blob-limit <mb>     Skip blobs larger than this size in MB (default: 5)
#   --content-types <ct>  ; separated content type prefixes to skip downloading (e.g. video/;audio/)
#   --timeout <sec>       Connect timeout in seconds (default: 30)
#   --keep-snapshots <n>  Compact backup once it has more than N snapshots (default: 14)
#
# Examples:
#   ./backup-create.sh ./backups/myws myws
#   ./backup-create.sh ./backups/myws myws --full-verify
#   ./backup-create.sh ./backups/myws myws --skip fulltext-blob

Everything is staged and verified. Here's the plan — I need your approval before anything billable is created.

## Huly on redu — deployment plan

**Source:** `hcengineering/huly-selfhost` (the supported self-host path — *not* the 732-line dev stack in `hcengineering/platform`), pinned to `HULY_VERSION=v0.7.426`.

| | |
|---|---|
| **VM** | `m1.mem16` — 4 vCPU / 16 GB / **40 GB disk** |
| **Cost** | **GBP 0.0556/hr ≈ GBP 40.59/month**, billed hourly |
| **URL** | `https://huly-i11spi8u.redu.cloud` (generated up front so `HOST_ADDRESS` matches) |
| **Stack** | 14 containers, port 80 via their nginx, redu terminating TLS |
| **Database** | none managed — CockroachDB runs *on the VM* |

**Three things to weigh before you say go:**

1. **This is above the no-card trial ceiling** (`m1.medium`). It needs a payment method. 4 vCPU/16 GB is upstream's *recommended* spec, not my guess — their README warns smaller servers may stop responding.
2. **Your data lives on the app VM.** redu has no managed CockroachDB or MinIO, so the database, files and search index sit on named volumes beside the app. `delete_deployment` destroys the workspace with it. The 40 GB disk is shared between all of that plus 14 images — that's the number upstream's "16 GB RAM" quote does *not* cover, and growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.
3. **Sign-up is open at boot.** There's no admin variable, so this is a two-phase deploy: I bring it up, immediately create your account, then set `DISABLE_SIGNUP=true` on `account` + `front` and prove it's closed with the RPC probe. The gap between "healthy" and "claimed" is a real window I'll keep to minutes — I won't stop at "the URL works".

**Fixes I applied to upstream's compose** (verified with `docker compose config`): `80:80` instead of the empty-variable publish; dropped kvs's unrouted `8094`; pinned MinIO off `:latest`; made `DISABLE_SIGNUP` flippable via `.env`. Plus one I found rather than read: **`redpanda` was the only one of 14 services with no `restart:` policy** — it's the queue all nine Huly services use, so a VM reboot would bring back 13 containers and leave the stack quietly broken. Added.

input.command:
cat > verify-signup-closed.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove public sign-up is really off on your Huly, without creating anything.
#   ./verify-signup-closed.sh huly-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed. 1 = OPEN, anyone can create an account right now. 2 = inconclusive, re-run.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-signup-closed.sh <host>}"
RPC="https://$HOST/_accounts"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

rpc_code() {   # $1 = method name. Body on stdin so nothing lands in ps.
  printf '{"method":"%s","params":{}}' "$1" \
    | curl -sS -o "$TMP/out" -w '%{http_code}' \
           -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- "$RPC"
}

# 1. GATE, and the POSITIVE CONTROL in one step. `login` is ALWAYS registered, so if it answers
#    404 we are not talking to Huly's account service and nothing below would mean anything.
code=$(rpc_code login)
case "$code" in
  200|400) echo "gate OK: the account RPC is answering and login is registered." ;;
  502)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from redu's proxy, the stack is still starting." >&2
    echo "  Fourteen containers take a while. Wait and re-run; this is NOT a pass." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  404)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: login itself answered 404, so this is not Huly's account endpoint." >&2
    echo "  Check the nginx route for /_accounts before reading anything into the next step." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  *) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected HTTP $code from the account RPC." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# 2. THE ASSERTION. With DISABLE_SIGNUP=true the method is not registered at all, so the service
#    answers 404 UnknownMethod. Anything else means it IS registered and open to the internet.
code=$(rpc_code signUp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ] && grep -qi 'method' "$TMP/out"; then
  echo "OK: signUp is not registered. Public sign-up is closed at the account service."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUp answered HTTP $code, so the method is still registered." >&2
  echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your server. Set DISABLE_SIGNUP=true" >&2
  echo "  on BOTH the account and front services and restart them, then re-run this." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 3. And the OTP variant, which is a separate method and is easy to forget.
code=$(rpc_code signUpOtp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
  echo "OK: signUpOtp is not registered either."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUpOtp answered HTTP $code and is still open." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Invites still work: signUpJoin stays registered on purpose."
EOF
chmod +x verify-signup-closed.sh && echo "staged verify-signup-closed.sh" && bash -n verify-signup-closed.sh && echo "syntax OK"

structuredContent.redu_md_markdown:
---
last_deploy:
  id: 513
  date: 2026-08-23
  status: ready
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/hcengineering/platform
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: hardcoreeng/front:v0.7.426 (plus account, transactor, workspace, collaborator, fulltext, rekoni, stats, kvs, and cockroach, redpanda, elastic, minio, nginx)
  port: 80
  vm: m1.mem16
  flavor_id: "7"
  database: none. Huly's datastore is CockroachDB, which redu does not offer managed, so it runs on the app VM on a named volume
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0556
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: huly
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ THE COMPOSE YOU WANT IS IN A DIFFERENT REPO FROM THE ONE THIS FILE CREDITS. hcengineering/platform is the source code, and dev/docker-compose.yaml in it is a 732-line DEVELOPMENT stack with a redpanda console and every optional service: do not deploy it. The supported self-host path is hcengineering/huly-selfhost, whose compose.yml is 281 lines and 14 active services, pinned by its .template.huly.conf to HULY_VERSION v0.7.426. Start there, and read MIGRATION.md in that repo before ever changing the version, because Huly upgrades sometimes need steps."
  - "⛔ IT FITS ON ONE VM, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES THE NUMBER, WHICH IS RARE. The huly-selfhost README says in its own words that Huly is resource-heavy: minimum 2 vCPU and 8 GB, recommended 4 vCPU and 16 GB or more, and that servers below the minimum may stop responding or fail. So m1.mem16 (4 vCPU / 16 GB) at GBP 0.0556/hr IS the recommended specification, not a guess, and m1.large would only meet the minimum for GBP 0.007/hr less. ⚠️ THE DISK IS THE PART THAT IS NOT COVERED BY THAT QUOTE: m1.mem16 comes with 40 GB, and this stack puts CockroachDB, an Elasticsearch index, a Redpanda log and every uploaded file on it, on top of fourteen images. Put that in front of the user BEFORE sizing, because growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy. This is far ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium: say so before the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO MANAGED DATABASE IN THIS RECIPE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Huly's datastore is CockroachDB, reached over the postgres wire, and redu has no managed CockroachDB. Substituting redu's managed Postgres is NOT a supported configuration: the platform ships a Cockroach-specific adapter for its communication subsystem (foundations/communication/packages/cockroach) and both documented deployments, compose and Helm, run CockroachDB. Do not test that substitution on someone's real workspace. Consequence to state plainly BEFORE they approve: apps, issues, documents and messages all live on the app VM's named volumes, so deleting the deployment deletes them. huly-selfhost ships backup-create.sh and backup-restore.sh; that is the backup story, and it is worth setting up on day one."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: PUBLIC SIGN-UP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT AND THE FIRST PERSON TO SIGN UP GETS AN ACCOUNT AND A WORKSPACE ON YOUR SERVER. There is no install wizard and no deploy-time admin variable, so this needs a TWO-PHASE deploy and you must not stop at 'the URL works'. Phase one: deploy with sign-up open, then IMMEDIATELY create the user's account, having confirmed the email address with them first. Phase two: set DISABLE_SIGNUP=true on BOTH the account AND the front service and restart those two containers. Verified in server/account-service/src/index.ts:137-138: that variable makes getMethods() omit signUp and signUpOtp entirely, so it is a real server-side closure and not a UI toggle, and invite-based joining (signUpJoin) keeps working. Upstream's own README says to create the initial account before disabling sign-ups. The window between healthy and claimed is real: keep it to minutes, and check the account list afterwards."
  - "⛔ SET SECURE AND HOST_ADDRESS OR THE APP LOADS AND THEN CANNOT CONNECT. Their compose builds every public URL with the shell trick http${SECURE:+s}://${HOST_ADDRESS}, so an EMPTY SECURE yields http:// and ws:// links. Behind redu's TLS the browser then blocks them as mixed content and you get a page that renders and never signs in, which reads as a broken deploy rather than a config mistake. Set SECURE=true and HOST_ADDRESS to the bare hostname with no scheme. Generate the dname yourself in the full huly-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so both are known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ SHIP .huly.nginx IN THE TARBALL. IT STARTS WITH A DOT. The compose bind-mounts ./.huly.nginx into the nginx container as its only server block, and it is a committed file in huly-selfhost rather than something generated at boot. If your upload misses dotfiles, nginx starts with the stock default site and every route 404s while all fourteen containers look healthy. Check the tarball actually contains it before deploying. That file is also where the routes live: / to front:8080, /_accounts, /_collaborator, /_transactor, /_rekoni, /_stats, with client_max_body_size 100M."
  - "PORT 80, THROUGH THEIR NGINX, AND NOTHING ELSE. Publish 80 on the host and pass port 80 to deploy_compose. ⚠️ Simplify their publish line: upstream writes \"${HTTP_BIND}:${HTTP_PORT}:80\" and relies on an EMPTY variable meaning all interfaces, which is a footgun in a file you are already editing. Write 80:80. Also DELETE the ports: block on the kvs service, which publishes 8094 on the host: nothing in .huly.nginx routes to it and no other service in this compose is given its URL, so it does not need to be reachable from outside the compose network at all."
  - "⛔ SET SECRET ONCE AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It is passed to every service as SERVER_SECRET or SECRET and it signs the tokens the browser, the transactor and the collaborator all present to each other. Two failure modes, and the second is the confusing one: change it and everybody is logged out; set it INCONSISTENTLY across services and the app loads, signs in, and then the transactor or the collaborator rejects the token, so documents will not open and it looks like a broken feature rather than a broken secret. Upstream's setup script generates it; on redu, generate one long random value yourself and put it in the project .env so every service interpolates the same one."
  - "PIN THE VERSION, AND KNOW WHY THE REGISTRY LOOKS NEWER THAN IT IS. Set HULY_VERSION=v0.7.426, which is the newest GitHub release (2026-07-05) and what huly-selfhost's own template pins. ⚠️ Docker Hub disagrees with GitHub in both directions: hardcoreeng/front carries v0.7.432 (2026-07-16) with NO matching GitHub release, and above that s0.7.433 to s0.7.437, which are STAGING builds. The huly-selfhost README is explicit that self-hosted deployments use v* tags. Do not reach for the newest-looking tag. The supporting images are pinned upstream too: cockroachdb/cockroach:latest-v24.2, redpandadata/redpanda:v24.3.6, elasticsearch:7.14.2, nginx:1.21.3. ⚠️ minio/minio has no tag in their compose, which means :latest, and the newest community MinIO tag on Docker Hub is from 2025-09-07: pin minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z rather than leaving it floating."
  - "PERSIST FIVE NAMED VOLUMES: cr_data and cr_certs (CockroachDB, which is everything), elastic (the search index, rebuildable but slow), files (MinIO: every uploaded document and attachment) and redpanda (the queue). Use NAMED volumes rather than the VOLUME_*_PATH bind-mount option their .conf offers, because a source re-upload replaces the project directory. Losing files loses attachments while the issues referencing them survive, which is the confusing failure; losing cr_data loses the product."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH BEFORE ANYONE SIGNS IN: the front-end bundle, the account service's JSON-RPC endpoint at /_accounts (which is how login and, until you close it, sign-up work), and the /_stats endpoint. MinIO is NOT routed by .huly.nginx and is not published, which is what makes the image-default MinIO credentials embedded in six STORAGE_CONFIG strings survivable rather than fatal. ⚠️ If you ever add a public route to MinIO, change those credentials FIRST, and remember they appear in all six strings, so a partial change breaks file uploads in exactly one service."
  - "IT IS FOURTEEN CONTAINERS AND THE FIRST BOOT IS LONG. Elasticsearch installs its ingest-attachment plugin on first start (their compose does it in the command), CockroachDB initialises its store, Redpanda formats its log, and only then do nine Huly services connect. Give the health check generous room and judge readiness by the account RPC answering, not by nginx answering: nginx is up long before the platform behind it is."
  - "ELASTICSEARCH TAKES 1 GB BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING. Their compose sets ES_JAVA_OPTS to -Xms1024m -Xmx1024m, so a full gigabyte of the VM is committed to the search JVM at boot. That is a large part of why upstream's minimum is 8 GB, and it is the first knob to turn if you ever need room, at the cost of full-text search performance."
  - "THE COMMENTED-OUT SERVICES ARE COMMENTED OUT FOR A REASON. compose.yml ships mongodb, redis and hulypulse disabled, and their comments say what each unlocks: mongo for the aibot and calendar services, redis for HulyPulse, HulyPulse for push notifications and real-time updates. Leave them off for a first deploy. Every one of them is another container on the same VM and the 16 GB above does not include them."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The workspace service runs Huly's own migrations, and the account service migrates its own schema at boot. Do not add a migration step of your own."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost (about GBP 0.056/hr, roughly GBP 41 a month, NOT inside the no-card trial), the fact that the data lives on the app VM and the two-phase sign-up close -> WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '7' (m1.mem16), NO managed database, port 80. # Self-host Huly on redu

An all-in-one project management platform (issues, documents, chat, HR, time tracking) on
infrastructure you own: Huly's own self-host stack, fourteen containers, on one memory-first VM
with a public HTTPS URL.

## What this deploys

- **Huly** from its official pinned images: front, account, transactor, workspace, collaborator,
  fulltext, rekoni, stats and kvs.
- **CockroachDB, MinIO, Elasticsearch and Redpanda** beside them, because they are Huly's database,
  file store, search index and queue, and redu offers no managed substitute for any of them.
- Their own nginx as the single ingress on port 80, with redu terminating TLS in front of it.
- Named volumes for all five datastores, and a public hostname on `*.redu.cloud`.

About GBP 0.0556/hour, roughly GBP 41 a month. **Well above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this
one needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Huly on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Two things to know before you approve the plan

**It really is resource-heavy, and upstream says so in its own README:** minimum 2 vCPU and 8 GB,
recommended 4 vCPU and 16 GB or more, with a warning that smaller servers may stop responding. The
flavor here is the recommended one rather than the minimum. The part that quote does not cover is
disk: 40 GB comes with it, shared between the database, the search index, the queue and every file
your team uploads.

**Your data lives on the app VM.** Huly stores everything in CockroachDB and MinIO, and redu has no
managed equivalent for either, so both run beside the app on named volumes. Deleting the deployment
deletes the workspace with it. Set up `backup-create.sh` from the huly-selfhost repository on day
one.

## The three that actually break it

**Sign-up is open.** There is no install wizard and no deploy-time admin variable. The first person
to find the URL can create an account and a workspace on your server. The recipe creates your
account immediately and then sets `DISABLE_SIGNUP=true`, which removes the sign-up methods from
the account service entirely rather than hiding a button.

**The scheme variable.** Every public URL is built as `http` plus an `s` only if `SECURE` is
non-empty. Leave it empty behind redu's TLS and the app renders and then silently fails to connect.

**The nginx file.** The single server block is a committed dotfile, `.huly.nginx`, bind-mounted
from the project directory. Miss it in the upload and every route 404s while every container looks
healthy.

## Prove sign-up is actually closed

Run this after phase two. It tests the behaviour rather than the flag: Huly's account service is
JSON-RPC over one endpoint, an unknown method answers **404** and a registered method that throws
answers **400**, so the two are distinguishable and the check cannot quietly pass.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove public sign-up is really off on your Huly, without creating anything.
#   ./verify-signup-closed.sh huly-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed. 1 = OPEN, anyone can create an account right now. 2 = inconclusive, re-run.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-signup-closed.sh <host>}"
RPC="https://$HOST/_accounts"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

rpc_code() {   # $1 = method name. Body on stdin so nothing lands in ps.
  printf '{"method":"%s","params":{}}' "$1" \
    | curl -sS -o "$TMP/out" -w '%{http_code}' \
           -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- "$RPC"
}

# 1. GATE, and the POSITIVE CONTROL in one step. `login` is ALWAYS registered, so if it answers
#    404 we are not talking to Huly's account service and nothing below would mean anything.
code=$(rpc_code login)
case "$code" in
  200|400) echo "gate OK: the account RPC is answering and login is registered." ;;
  502)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from redu's proxy, the stack is still starting." >&2
    echo "  Fourteen containers take a while. Wait and re-run; this is NOT a pass." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  404)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: login itself answered 404, so this is not Huly's account endpoint." >&2
    echo "  Check the nginx route for /_accounts before reading anything into the next step." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  *) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected HTTP $code from the account RPC." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# 2. THE ASSERTION. With DISABLE_SIGNUP=true the method is not registered at all, so the service
#    answers 404 UnknownMethod. Anything else means it IS registered and open to the internet.
code=$(rpc_code signUp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ] && grep -qi 'method' "$TMP/out"; then
  echo "OK: signUp is not registered. Public sign-up is closed at the account service."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUp answered HTTP $code, so the method is still registered." >&2
  echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your server. Set DISABLE_SIGNUP=true" >&2
  echo "  on BOTH the account and front services and restart them, then re-run this." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 3. And the OTP variant, which is a separate method and is easy to forget.
code=$(rpc_code signUpOtp)
if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
  echo "OK: signUpOtp is not registered either."
else
  echo "FAIL: signUpOtp answered HTTP $code and is still open." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Invites still work: signUpJoin stays registered on purpose."
```
